A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 17 pages of v2 and 21 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, were readable and supported comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original transformer-training experiments, pretraining and representation-similarity results, and recursion/generalization tests in Sections 4–6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds further learning curves and ABC Grammar alignment results, including Table 4 in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The nanoGPT-based architectures, autoregressive training objective, and subgrammar-pretraining followed by full-grammar training procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same architectural and optimizer specifications.

E1.justification: V3 first names and defines PythonPCFG, assigning it to the numerically unchanged Table 1, whose grammar v2 did not identify. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether Python-like coverage is newly added or newly documented. The other grammar families and arithmetic tasks are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons retain training from scratch, subgrammar pretraining followed by full training, and pretraining-only reference conditions. New Table 4 uses these existing comparison types; newly cited research does not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The infix/suffix plots change their displayed pretraining boundaries and total minibatch ranges between v2 Figure 5 and v3 Figure 3. New Table 4 reports small two-layer models with 2 or 4 pretraining epochs followed by 10 full-grammar epochs. Other newly stated details of retained experiments are disclosures rather than established protocol changes.

E4.justification: The subgrammar-location analysis gains a prefix-pretraining case and revised infix/suffix trajectories. Table 4 extends the representation analysis to short pretraining durations on ABC Grammar, examining 2 versus 4 epochs. These are limited extensions of existing retention and pretraining-sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: V2 already reports 30 seeds. V3 additionally specifies averaging CKA over 435 distinct off-diagonal seed pairs in Appendix B and the table captions. This adds seed-aggregation information without establishing additional runs or introducing confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds mixture-grammar curves in Figure 1b, a prefix-pretraining curve, replacement infix/suffix trajectories, and Table 4. The latter reports full-grammar attention CKA of 0.208 from scratch versus 0.220 with two pretraining epochs. Tables 1 and 3 remain numerically unchanged; the revised training curves do not establish matched-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 revises probability terms in the motivating derivation from P_G(a) to P_A(a) and P_G(a|alpha), and adds an explicit factorization step. Theorem 4.3's appendix proof also receives indexing and expression refinements. The main theorem statements and assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The principal claims about recursive loss decomposition, conditional parallel learning, tiny-model pretraining benefits, and representation alignment remain. Although v3 shortens the abstract and reduces emphasis on recursion difficulty in the closing discussion, that finding remains in the introduction and Section 6.

C2.justification: V3 Appendix E.4 replaces v2's assertion that deeply nested valid prefixes degrade performance more than malformed prefixes with an interpretation of nearly identical curves and minimal prefix influence. Appendix B adds that CKA cannot identify specific shared features. Section 6 removes the explicit caution against interpreting anecdotal arithmetic tests as evidence about training difficulty.

D1.justification: V3 substantially expands reproducibility information: it supplies a code-access link, details activation collection, token aggregation and centering for CKA, documents matched training budgets and additional training epochs, and provides the previously unspecified PythonPCFG productions. These fill important gaps in documenting the retained empirical work.

R1.justification: V3 sharpens its stated distinction from Cagnetta and Wyart concerning recursive grammars, final-token prediction, and parallel versus staged learning. It also adds references and discussion on structural pre-pretraining and depth generalization. The overall positioning around subgrammar learning remains intact.

P1.justification: Editing concentrates on the abstract, Sections 5.2, 6 and 7, and explanations accompanying the grammars. V3 adds a CKA appendix and Impact Statement and corrects author information and typos. The main section sequence and much of the exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a two-panel display. V2's appendix Figure 5 moves into the main text as Figure 3, gains a prefix panel, and uses redrawn plots. V3 also adds Table 4 and expands captions; most other displays retain their structure despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the empirical work easier to assess and reproduce through the grammar specification, detailed CKA procedure, training-budget disclosures, and code-access link. Additional alignment results and a prefix interpretation consistent with the plots also help. The gains chiefly concern documentation and limited empirical extensions; removing the explicit arithmetic-test caution slightly weakens qualification.
